findings.title: Re-entry guard does not actually protect the documented "rapid Try Again tap" path because reset() clears the processing flag first
findings.explanation: The guard comment at ScreenshotTranslationStore.swift:163-165 explicitly claims it stops "a rapid 'Try Again' tap" from starting a parallel pipeline. But the Try Again handler calls store.reset() BEFORE await store.processScreenshots(). reset() (lines 215-220) unconditionally sets state = .idle. So for the Try Again path the guard at line 166 sees .idle and always proceeds; the flag it relies on has just been cleared by the same handler. In a double-tap window (two taps landing while state == .error, before Task1 sets state = .stitching and the view re-renders away from errorView), Task1 runs reset->stitching->await(suspend), then Task2 runs reset()->idle->guard passes->second pipeline. The guard genuinely DOES protect the primary intent-refire path (the intent perform() never calls reset()), so concurrent pipelines are prevented there. Practical reachability of the Try Again race is very low because the error view (and thus the button) is replaced by processingView as soon as state becomes .stitching, so a human second tap almost always misses the button. Reporting as a nit: the code/comment overclaim is real, the practical impact is minimal.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the guard authoritative by moving the stale-result clearing INSIDE processScreenshots() after the guard, and drop the external reset() from the Try Again handler. E.g. after `guard !state.isProcessing else { return }` set stitchedResult/recognizedBlocks/translatedBlocks = nil, then change the button to just `Task { await store.processScreenshots() }`. Since the guard already passes for the .error state (error is not isProcessing), Try Again still works, and the processing flag can no longer be bypassed by an external reset(). Alternatively, narrow the comment to claim protection only for the intent-refire case.

findings.title: DeepSeek reasoner is sent max_completion_tokens, but DeepSeek's API uses max_tokens
findings.explanation: isReasoningModel returns true for any model id containing "reasoner" (e.g. the default `deepseek-reasoner`), and the reasoning branch then sets ONLY `body["max_completion_tokens"] = maxTokens`, omitting `max_tokens` entirely. This token-limit param substitution is required for OpenAI's o-series (which rejects `max_tokens`), but DeepSeek is a separate provider routed through the same openAICompatible path (AIProvider.deepseek defaults to .openAICompatible, base https://api.deepseek.com/v1). DeepSeek's documented output-limit parameter for deepseek-reasoner is `max_tokens`; `max_completion_tokens` is not a DeepSeek parameter. Net effect: the app's intended token cap (2048 for translate, 4096 for chat) is no longer delivered to DeepSeek under a name it recognizes, so the cap is silently dropped (DeepSeek falls back to its own default), and if DeepSeek's gateway is strict about unknown fields the request could be rejected outright. This is a behavior regression specific to deepseek-reasoner: the previous code (`max_tokens` + `temperature`) worked because DeepSeek honors `max_tokens` and silently ignores `temperature` for the reasoner. Dropping `temperature` is correct for DeepSeek; switching the token param name is not.
findings.suggestedFix: Split the reasoning branch by family rather than applying max_completion_tokens to everything. Keep omitting temperature for all reasoning models, but use max_completion_tokens only for the OpenAI o-series and max_tokens for DeepSeek-style reasoners. For example: `if isReasoningModel(model) { if isOpenAIOSeries(model) { body["max_completion_tokens"] = maxTokens } else { body["max_tokens"] = maxTokens } } else { body["temperature"] = 0.3; body["max_tokens"] = maxTokens }`, where isOpenAIOSeries is the existing o+digit check and the reasoner (non-o-series) path keeps max_tokens.

findings.title: GPT-5 family not treated as a reasoning model (would send rejected temperature/max_tokens)
findings.explanation: isReasoningModel only matches o-series ('o'+digit) and 'reasoner'. OpenAI's gpt-5 family also requires max_completion_tokens and rejects a non-default temperature, but because those ids start with 'g' they take the else branch and are sent `temperature: 0.3` + `max_tokens`, which OpenAI would 400. This is out of the explicitly-listed audit scope and gpt-5 is not in AIProvider.openAI.defaultModels (gpt-4o, gpt-4.1, gpt-4.1-mini, o4-mini, o3, gpt-4o-mini), so it only bites if a user manually types a gpt-5 id; reporting for completeness since it is the same defect class the fix targets.
